There is a printer's imprint in the lower right. OCR reads it roughly as 'Теодоръ Киббель' but not reliably enough to record as fact.

Album cover::Youngblood Brass Band - Pax.verified_against: Timothy J. Reynolds' own portfolio at turnislefthome.com, on his page for this cover: 'Art & Sons, a small studio out of Madison, WI commissioned me to [re]design the cover art for Youngblood Brass Band'. The image here is served from that same Wix site. The release itself is confirmed on Discogs — Youngblood Brass Band, Pax Volumi, Tru Thoughts, UK, 2013 (TRUCD278 / TRULP278, master 680660).
notes: Credited as ILLUSTRATOR, not designer. Reynolds states plainly on his own page that he 'didn't design any packaging/graphic design/etc' — only the illustration. The archive keeps that distinction.
The work was a commissioned RE-design: Art & Sons brought him in to reinterpret cover art the band had outgrown.

A web summary credited the original art to 'Scott Pauli and Tim Reynolds'. Reynolds' own page does not mention Pauli, so Pauli is not credited here — the earlier artwork's authorship is left open rather than guessed at.
No Discogs pressing of this release carries an art or design credit at all, on any of the four; the attribution comes entirely from the illustrator's own site.

Image is the untransformed Wix master at 1394x1478. The URL Todd sent carried a w_2500 transform but actually served 1254x1330 at a fifth of the bytes — on Wix the master sits at the bare /media/ path, and the dimensions are encoded in the filename.

deadlypreygallery.com::akira::heavy-j.title: Akira
deadlypreygallery.com::akira::heavy-j.subtitle: Hand-painted Ghanaian mobile cinema poster
deadlypreygallery.com::akira::heavy-j.verified_against: Deadly Prey Gallery, the Chicago dealer that works directly with these painters, lists this as "AKIRA (High Quality Print) - Heavy J" and describes it as "the legendary Ghanaian artist Heavy J's incredible version of classic animated Japanese film Akira", printed from the original painting at approximately 14 x 20.5 inches.
notes: Hand-painted poster in the tradition of Ghana's mobile cinema banners, which were painted on recycled flour sacks to advertise travelling video screenings. Deadly Prey Gallery commissions new work from these painters, so this is a painting in that tradition; the gallery does not say it was used on the video-club circuit, and this record does not claim it was.
The painting carries the lettering "Manso Video Mamobi" — Mamobi is a neighbourhood of Accra — alongside the artist's stamp at lower left.
No date is recorded. The gallery gives none and none is legible on the painting, so the year is left blank rather than inferred from the film's 1988 release.

The image is the gallery's reproduction of the original painting, cropped to the painted area — their print carries the gallery's logo and the artist's stamp on the white margin below, which are not part of the painting.
